summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and a tracheostomy was admitted from his nursing facility with fever and tachycardia. Initial evaluation revealed leukocytosis and a urinalysis positive for nitrites and white blood cells. A chest X-ray showed increased interstitial markings without pneumonia. Urine culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Enterococcus species, leading to a diagnosis of urinary tract infection with sepsis. He was treated with cefepime and linezolid after a PICC line was placed. His condition improved, and he remained afebrile. Chronic conditions including HIV, seizures, COPD, and abdominal pain were managed with home medications. Citalopram was held due to interaction risk with linezolid. He was discharged back to extended care with plans to complete a two-week course of IV and oral antibiotics and follow up on his SVT and medication reconciliation.
